terms.definition: A team member in the chasing turn whose goal is to tag out the runners. 8 chasers sit in alternating directions on squares, 1 is the active chaser.
A player from the opposing team who must dodge the active chaser and avoid being tagged. 3 runners enter per batch.
The act of touching a sitting teammate on the back while loudly saying 'Kho', transferring the role of active chaser.
The single chaser currently permitted to run, pursue runners, and give 'Kho' to sitting teammates.
Cylindrical wooden poles at each end of the central lane (1.20–1.25m tall). The Free Zone behind the post allows the active chaser to change direction.
A 24m long, 30cm wide lane running down the center of the court between the two posts.
One of 8 lanes perpendicular to the central lane where chasers sit in their squares.
Each match has 2 innings. In each inning, teams alternate between chasing turn (9 minutes) and running turn (9 minutes).
A group of 3 runners that enters the field simultaneously. After all 3 are dismissed, the next batch enters.
